title: Integral Chow envelope with reduced projective compactification
statement: Let $S$ be an affine Noetherian scheme (affine and locally Noetherian [def-weil-affine-spectrum, pqf-def-locnoeth]), and let $f:R\to S$ be separated and of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with $R$ integral [def-pc-integral-scheme], generic point $\xi$ [def-sc-generic-point], and function field $L=\kappa(\xi)$ [def-sc-function-field]. There exist $n\geq0$, integral Noetherian schemes $Y,Z$, a proper surjective morphism $\pi:Y\to R$ [def-weil-surjective-morphism], an immersion $j:Y\to P=\mathbf P^n_S$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], a closed immersion $c:Z\to P$, and a dense open immersion $e:Y\to Z$ [def-weil-open-immersion], all over $S$, with $j=c\circ e$. The morphism $Z\to S$ is proper, and $c(Z)$ is the closure of $j(Y)$ in $P$, endowed with its reduced induced closed subscheme structure [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. There is a nonempty dense open $U\subseteq R$ such that $\pi^{-1}(U)\to U$ is an isomorphism. Via this isomorphism and $e$, both function fields $k(Y)$ and $k(Z)$ identify with $L$, and the composites of their canonical generic-point maps with $\pi$ and $j$ are respectively the canonical map $\operatorname{Spec}L\to R$ and its image in $P$.

source.place: Tag 0208, limits-lemma-Noetherian-dvr-valuative-proper, proof of (4) implies (1), Chow envelope and projective closure; integral refinement by reduced closure of the generic preimage. Chow input: coherent.tex Tag 0200, coherent-lemma-chow-Noetherian.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-chow-noetherian] to $f:R\to S$. It gives $n\geq0$, $q:T\to R$ proper and surjective, an $S$-immersion $a:T\to P=\mathbf P^n_S$, and a dense open $U\subseteq R$ over which $q$ is an isomorphism. By [def-weil-proper-morphism], $q$ is of finite type. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] first to $R\to S$ and then to $T\to R$: both $R$ and $T$ are Noetherian. Since $R$ is integral, it is nonempty, so its dense open $U$ is nonempty.

Put $W=q^{-1}(U)$, identified with $U$. It is a nonempty integral open subscheme of $T$: nonempty opens of an irreducible space are irreducible, and restriction preserves reducedness. Use [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] to give $\overline{|W|}\subseteq T$ its reduced induced closed structure $b:Y\hookrightarrow T$. The closure of the irreducible nonempty space $W$ is irreducible and nonempty. Thus $Y$ is integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme].

The restriction $b^{-1}(W)\to W$ is a reduced closed subscheme with underlying space all of $W$. Indeed restricting its affine quotient presentation just localizes the quotient rings, and localizations of reduced rings are reduced. Since $W$ itself is reduced, uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] identifies this restriction with $W$ itself. Consequently, for $\pi=q\circ b$, one has $\pi^{-1}(U)\cong W\cong U$. Also $W$ is dense in $Y$ by the definition of $Y$'s underlying space.

source.place: Tag 01J3, schemes-lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme, uniqueness and affine quotient description

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], $b$ is proper and $\pi=q\circ b$ is proper, since $q$ is proper. Its image is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-closed-image] and contains $U$, so it is all of $R$; hence $\pi$ is surjective. The finite-type clause of properness and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] applied to $b:Y\to T$ show that $Y$ is Noetherian.

Set $j=a\circ b$. To check that this is an immersion, factor $a$ as a closed immersion $T\hookrightarrow V$ followed by an open immersion $V\hookrightarrow P$, as in [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The composite $Y\hookrightarrow T\hookrightarrow V$ is closed: on affine opens it is the composite of two surjective quotient-ring maps, which is surjective, and its underlying image is closed. Thus $j$ has the required closed-then-open factorization. As $a$ is over $S$, so is $j$, with structure map $f\circ\pi$.

source.place: Tag 01QO, morphisms-lemma-closed-immersion; closed-then-open definition of immersion

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] again, now on the closed subset $\overline{j(Y)}\subseteq P$, to obtain $c:Z\hookrightarrow P$. Its underlying space is nonempty irreducible, being the closure of the image of integral $Y$, and $Z$ is reduced; hence $Z$ is integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Here $P=\mathbf P^n_S$ is $\mathbf P(\{0,\ldots,n\};S)$ by [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]: the finite index set has $n+1$ homogeneous coordinates, including when $n=0$. Apply [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper] with this index set to obtain properness of $P\to S$, so $Z\to S$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to $P\to S$ and to $c:Z\to P$, using the finite-type clause of properness, to see that $P$ and $Z$ are Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 01J3, schemes-lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme; morphisms.tex Tags 01WC, morphisms-lemma-locally-projective-proper; 01W5, morphisms-lemma-closed-immersion-proper; 01T6, morphisms-lemma-finite-type-noetherian

proof.text: Use the factorization $j:Y\hookrightarrow V\hookrightarrow P$ of step 5. Because $j(Y)$ is closed in the open $V$, one has $\overline{j(Y)}\cap V=j(Y)$. The restriction $c^{-1}(V)\to V$ is a reduced closed subscheme with this image. So is $Y\to V$. Uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] gives an isomorphism $Y\cong c^{-1}(V)$ over $V$, hence over $P$. Follow it by the open inclusion $c^{-1}(V)\hookrightarrow Z$ to define $e$. By [def-weil-open-immersion], $e$ is open, and by construction $c\circ e=j$. It is dense because $c(Z)=\overline{j(Y)}$, and it is over $S$ because its composite with $c$ is $j$.

source.place: Tag 01J3, schemes-lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme, uniqueness; reduced-closure version of morphisms.tex Tag 01RG, morphisms-lemma-quasi-compact-immersion

proof.text: The generic point $\xi$ of $R$ lies in $U$: every nonempty open meets the dense singleton $\{\xi\}$ by [def-sc-generic-point]. Its inverse image in $W\cong U$ is a generic point $\eta$ of $Y$, since $W$ is dense; its image $\zeta=e(\eta)$ is generic in $Z$, since $e(Y)$ is dense. Open immersions induce isomorphisms on local rings by [def-weil-open-immersion]. The isomorphism $W\cong U$ and the two open inclusions therefore identify $\mathcal O_{Z,\zeta}$ with $\mathcal O_{Y,\eta}$ and with $\mathcal O_{R,\xi}$. These are $k(Z),k(Y),L$, respectively, by the integral-scheme convention of [def-sc-function-field].

source.place: Tag 01RW, morphisms-definition-function-field and the preceding generic-stalk description; limits.tex Tag 0208, limits-lemma-Noetherian-dvr-valuative-proper, identification of generic fields

proof.text: Under precisely those stalk identifications, write $g_Y:\operatorname{Spec}L\to Y$, $g_Z:\operatorname{Spec}L\to Z$, and $g_R:\operatorname{Spec}L\to R$ for the canonical generic-point maps. On any affine neighbourhood, each is induced by the section-to-generic-germ homomorphism into $L$. The maps just used on stalks are induced by these same germ homomorphisms, so functoriality of $\operatorname{Spec}$ gives $\pi g_Y=g_R$ and $e g_Y=g_Z$. Hence $j g_Y=c g_Z$. This explicitly gives the claimed canonical generic-point compatibility in $R$ and $P$, as well as the function-field identifications; every constructed morphism is over $S$.
